content: An inhaler, also known as a puffer, is a medical device designed to deliver medication directly into the body through the lungs. It is primarily used in the management and treatment of respiratory conditions such as asthma and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). The medication is typically stored in a pressurized canister in liquid form. This canister is connected to a plastic, hand-operated actuator. For instance, a metered-dose inhaler (MDI) releases a precise, pre-measured dose of medication in aerosol form when activated. To use an MDI correctly, the patient should first exhale completely, then place the mouthpiece of the inhaler into their mouth. As they begin to inhale, they should press down on the canister to release the medication. The aerosolized medication is then drawn into the lungs as the patient continues to inhale deeply. After inhalation, the patient should hold their breath for approximately 10 seconds to allow the medication to be absorbed into the bronchial walls. Alternatively, a spacer device can be used in conjunction with the inhaler. A spacer is an enclosed plastic chamber that mixes the medication with air, simplifying the process and ensuring the patient receives the full dose of the drug. This is particularly beneficial for individuals who may have difficulty coordinating their breathing with the activation of the inhaler. The largest manufacturers of inhalers include GlaxoSmithKline (producers of the Advair Diskus, a dry powder inhaler), Merck, AstraZeneca (makers of Pulmicort and Symbicort), and Boehringer Ingelheim (producers of Atrovent, Combivent, and Spiriva). These companies also produce the medications delivered via inhalers. Additionally, 3M Drug Delivery Systems plays a significant role in the production of finished inhaler products, as they are a leading manufacturer of MDI canisters, metering valves, and other essential components.
